reason: Both satisfy all hard constraints (headings, exactly 5 bullets, word count, honest counterargument, final sentence), but Response B organizes its five bullets as a coherent, actionable list under 'The proposal' and keeps 'What could go wrong' as pure prose that more substantively engages the objection (concrete flaky-test rate, causal reasoning, plus a secondary risk); Response A's bullet placement feels forced, splitting one problem stat into an isolated bullet and tacking on an unrelated friction point at the end of the risk section seemingly just to hit the bullet count.
